newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka air force plane explodes, pilot ejects.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka air force plane explodes, pilot ejects.

text.p: An air force Pucara ground attack aircraft exploded in midair and crashed in northeastern Sri Lanka but the pilot ejected safely, a military spokesman said on Sunday.
The Pucara was on a mission to engage a large Tamil Tiger rebel force on Saturday night when it lost radio contact with its base, Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters.
The wreckage of the aircraft was found in the Polonnaruwa district, 180 km (113 miles) from Colombo, he said.

"Soldiers at an army detachment in the area reported seeing a bright light and hearing an explosion in the air," he said. "The plane was flying at an altitude of 10,000 feet (about 3,000 metres). The pilot ejected and was picked up by helicopter uninjured. The cause of the crash is not known yet."
It was the sixth aircraft to be lost by the Indian Ocean island's tiny air force this year in operations against Tamil Tiger separatist rebels.

Rebels blew up a Y-12 transport plane at the China Bay airbase in eastern Trincomalee in early March while in February an An-32 transport plane crashed while taking off from an airbase near Colombo, killing three servicemen and wounding 36.

In January, a Kfir fighter jet crashed when the pilot ejected safely soon after takeoff from the Katunaike airbase, just north of Colombo, while a Y-12 transport plane and an unmanned drone, both on reconnaissance missions over northern waters, went missing the same month.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
